### Observed differences

- The clearest difference concerns how often A15 and A16 repeat. In both windows every case contained A15 and A16, but in the later window each averaged about 1.55 occurrences per case instead of about 1.7, and cases in which the activity repeated fell from about 40 in 100 to about 33 in 100; these are the largest occurrence differences in the sample and exceed about 92 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled cases. [OCC015, OCC016]
- The directly-follows profiles match a shorter back-and-forth between A15 and A16: A16 returned to A15 after about 35% of its outgoing transitions in the later window versus about 40% before, while its exits to A41 rose from about 30% to 34% and to A18 from about 12% to 16%; A15 still continued to A16 in about 98–99% of its transitions in both windows, but the observed outgoing transitions of A15 and A16 fell from 343 to 310 and from 344 to 311, the same relative drop as their occurrences. [DIR015, DIR016]
- Activity shifted between the A43/A44 exchange and A45/A46: A44 appeared in about 65 in 100 later cases versus about 59 before, while A45 and A46 each appeared in about 62 in 100 versus about 66; among A43's outgoing transitions, A44 rose from about 43% to 49% and A45 fell from about 55% to 49%, and among A44's outgoing transitions, A43 rose from about 35% to 40% while A47 fell from about 63% to 56%. [OCC043, OCC044, OCC045, DIR043, DIR044]
- After A14, cases continued to A15 more often (about 35% to 43% of A14's outgoing transitions) and to A04 less often (about 64% to 57%); A04 itself appeared in about 59 in 100 later cases versus about 67 before. [DIR014, OCC004]
- Several other branch choices moved by a few percentage points of outgoing transitions: A01 to A05 up (about 33% to 44%) with A01 to A07 down (about 36% to 26%); A12 to A13 up (about 22% to 33%) with A12 to A11 down (about 40% to 29%); A03 to A11 up (about 27% to 38%); A23 to A21 up (about 15% to 25%); A38 to A37 up (about 28% to 36%). [DIR001, DIR003, DIR012, DIR023, DIR038]
- Differences at rarely occurring activities (A02, A06, A08, A10, A48) look large in profile terms but rest on very few observations — for example A48 had one observed outgoing transition before versus seven after — and cannot be interpreted on this sample. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC008, OCC010, DIR002, DIR006, DIR008, DIR010, DIR048]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the alternating repetition of A15 and A16 ran fewer rounds per case: both activities still appeared in every case, but each averaged about 1.55 occurrences per case instead of about 1.7, repeats appeared in about 33 in 100 cases instead of about 40, and A16 more often left the pair to A41 or A18 instead of returning to A15. This is a change in how often an existing repetition executes, with participation unchanged at every case in both windows. The occurrence profiles of the two activities agree and rank around the 92nd percentile of random re-splits, and the directly-follows profiles show the matching exit redistribution and transition counts, so the hypothesis is shown directly and consistently. Limitations: the evidence contains no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with the number expected without a change, and a moderate sampling fluctuation in repetition counts remains a competing explanation that cannot be fully excluded. [OCC015, OCC016, DIR015, DIR016]

Other differences: A44 took place in more cases (about 59 to 65 in 100) while A45 and A46 took place in fewer (about 66 to 62), with A43's next step shifting from A45 toward A44 and A44's from A47 toward A43 [OCC043, OCC044, OCC045, DIR043, DIR044]; after A14, cases more often continued to A15 and less often to A04, and A04 appeared in fewer cases [DIR014, OCC004]; several other branch shares moved by a few percentage points at A01, A03, A12, A23 and A38 [DIR001, DIR003, DIR012, DIR023, DIR038]; profile changes at rare activities (A02, A06, A08, A10, A48) rest on too few observations to interpret [DIR002, DIR006, DIR008, DIR010, DIR048].
